result.topic_en: Formula-only notes on the zeta function: its Euler product, its integral representation via the Gamma function, the contour-integral form and its values at s=0 and negative even integers, the logarithmic derivative written as a sum over prime powers and its Möbius-type inversion leading to the logarithmic integral, and numerical values of Li at powers of 10 together with square-root calculations.
result.transcription:
$\int \frac{e^x dx}{x} = \frac{e^x}{x} + \int \frac{e^x dx}{x^2}$
$= e^x\left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^2} \cdots + \frac{(n-1)!}{x^n}\right) + \int \frac{e^x n!\, dx}{x^{n+1}}$
$\int \frac{e^x n!\, dx}{x^{n+1}} = \int e^x \int_0^\infty e^{-sx} s^n ds$ [?] $\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{(1-s)x} s^n}{1-s}$ [?] $\cdots$
$\sum \frac{1}{n^s} = \prod \frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{p^s}}$ $\quad s>1$
$\log \sum \frac{1}{n^s} = -\sum \log\left(1-\frac{1}{p^s}\right)$
$\cdots - \frac{p^{-s}\log p}{1-p^{-s}} \cdots =$ [?]

$\frac{\Pi(s-1)}{n^s} = \int_0^\infty e^{-nx} x^{s-1} dx$
$\sum \frac{\Pi(s-1)}{n^s} = \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-x}}{1-e^{-x}} x^{s-1} dx = \Pi(s-1)\,\zeta(s) = \int_0^\infty \frac{x^{s-1} dx}{e^x-1}$
$\chi(s) = \frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)} = -\sum \frac{\log p}{p^s-1} = -\sum p^{-s}\log p - \sum p^{-2s}\log p - \sum p^{-3s}\log p$
$\chi(s) - \chi(2s) - \chi(3s) - \chi(5s) + \chi(6s) - \chi(7s) + \chi(10s) - \chi(11s) = -\sum p^{-s}\log p$
$-\frac{1}{s-1} + \frac{1}{2s-1} + \frac{1}{3s-1} + \frac{1}{5s-1} \cdots = -\sum p^{-s}\log p$
$= -\int\left(x^{-s} - \frac{1}{2}x^{-s-\frac{1}{2}} - \frac{1}{3}x^{-s-\frac{2}{3}} - \frac{1}{5}x^{-s-\frac{4}{5}}\right)dx$

$\int_1^\infty x^{-s} dx = \frac{x^{1-s}}{1-s} \quad \frac{1}{1-s}$
$= \frac{1}{s-1} + \cdots$

$\int \frac{1}{\log x}\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}} - \frac{1}{3}x^{-\frac{2}{3}} - \frac{1}{5}x^{-\frac{4}{5}}\right)dx = Li\, x - \frac{1}{2}Li\, x^{\frac{1}{2}} - \frac{1}{3}Li\, x^{\frac{1}{3}} - \frac{1}{5}Li\, x^{\frac{1}{5}} + \frac{1}{6}Li\, x^{\frac{1}{6}} - \frac{1}{7}Li\, x^{\frac{1}{7}}$
$= \int \frac{dx}{\log x} - \int \frac{dx^{\frac{1}{2}}}{2\log x^{\frac{1}{2}}} - \int \frac{dx^{\frac{1}{3}}}{3\log x^{\frac{1}{3}}}$
